newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-NEW SOUTH WALES OVERWHELM FREE STATE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NEW SOUTH WALES OVERWHELM FREE STATE.

text.p: New South Wales breathed life into their Super 12 campaign with a convincing 36-11 win over Free State on Saturday to stay in contention for a semifinal berth.
The Waratahs earned a maximum five competition points from an enthralling match at the Sydney Football Stadium to move into sixth place on the Super 12 table on 16 points from six games.
Free State made a strong contribution to an open, attacking encounter but their hopes were dashed by a combination of poor finishing and resolute defence by the home side.
New South Wales captain and second rower Tim Gavin praised his fellow forwards for resisting the South Africans during a crucial period of pressure in the second half.
"The pack really took it to Free State and I think we got on top them. Our defensive effort was first rate," said Gavin, whose side ran in five tries to one.
On several occasions during the second half defenders stopped Free State just short of the line when a try would have brought the visitors back into the match.
New South Wales opened brightly when winger Alistair Murdoch capitalised on a Free State mistake to race to the line unchallenged in the third minute.
Matthew Burke displayed outstanding skill to extend the lead three minutes later when the Wallaby full-back twice kicked the ball forward off the ground to give centre Richard Tombs a simple try.
Burke added 11 points with his boot by landing four conversions and one penalty.
Free State recovered their poise when winger Stephen Brink narrowed the deficit by finishing off a move by diving over near the corner flag in the 12th minute.
Veteran winger David Campese restored New South Wales' advantage after exchanging passes with Tombs in an intricate move in front of the posts before diving over.
Leading 22-11 at halftime, scrum-half Sam Payne and flanker Michael Brial added further tries to seal New South Wales' victory.

Free State's hopes of getting back into contention disappeared when full-back Jorrie Kruger was adjudged to have slid into touch before grounding the ball with his side trailing 29-11 in the 58th minute. Televison replays suggested the try may have been valid.

New South Wales - Matt Burke, Alistair Murdoch, Graeme Bond, Richard Tombs, David Campese, Scott Bowen, Sam Payne, Fili Finau, Stu Pinkerton, Michael Brial, Sam Domoni, Tim Gavin (captain), Andrew Heath, Mark Bell, Richard Harry.

Free State - Jorrie Kruger, Jan-Harm van Wyk, Helgard Muller (captain), Brendan Venter, Stephen Brink, M.J. Smith, Werner Swanepoel, Johan Erasmus, Charl van Rensburg, Andre Venter, Braam Els, Ryno Opperman, Dougie Heymans, Naka Drotske, Pieter 'Os' du Randt.
